required_cases.given: a draft RuntimeRevision without any Route or ExecutionBinding
required_cases.when: the Publication runner probes the candidate RuntimeAdapter
expect: probeCapabilities returns a structurally valid capability manifest
protocol_versions and feature booleans and numeric limits are present
no platform object (Route, Binding, Invocation, Event, Tool, Memory, Child Thread) is required

required_cases.given: a draft RuntimeRevision and no business Invocation
required_cases.when: startInvocation is invoked exactly once on the candidate adapter
expect: startInvocation is invoked exactly once (no duplicate dispatch calls)
the adapter returns accepted=true
runtime_execution_ref and runtime_session_ref are unique and non-empty
the returned capabilities exactly match the suite's single probe snapshot
the acknowledgement is produced by the real adapter, not fabricated

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision advertised as cancellable
required_cases.when: handleCancel is invoked on the candidate adapter
expect: the adapter returns cancel_state=accepted (a real acknowledgement)
already_completed_effects_preserved is a boolean
cancel is a base publication capability and must actually ack

required_cases.given: the adapter capability manifest advertises a steer feature
expect: if features.steer is true, handleSteer returns accepted at next_safe_point
if features.steer is false, the runner only verifies steer is not advertised
no steer command is fabricated when the capability is absent

required_cases.given: the adapter capability manifest advertises a resume feature
expect: if features.resume is true, handleResume returns accepted
if features.resume is false, the runner only verifies resume is not advertised
no resume command is fabricated when the capability is absent

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision resumes a session
required_cases.when: the Publication runner verifies session recovery declaration
expect: if the workspace profile does not declare CHECKPOINT_RESTORABLE, the runner only verifies it is not advertised
if CHECKPOINT_RESTORABLE is declared, the runner performs a real resume probe carrying a checkpointRef
when CHECKPOINT_RESTORABLE is declared, handleResume must return accepted with non-empty remote refs
otherwise the case is fail-closed (the adapter does not claim filesystem-level recovery it cannot provide)

required_cases.when: the Publication runner performs a real startInvocation and inspects the acceptance receipt
expect: features.heartbeat is declared true
the acknowledgement carries a real acceptedAt inside the [dispatch, ack] window, so the platform can derive a lease expiry and detect stop-after-expiry

the acknowledgement is bound to the published capability manifest digest computed from (runtimeRevisionId, frozen capability manifest) — the same comparison source used by runtime-start, runtime-resume, ingress-runtime-events and the in-process hosted runtime
a fixed or fabricated acceptedAt fails the case; platform-side lease renewal and stop-after-expiry are proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision started twice with the same intent and once with changed content
required_cases.when: the Publication runner repeats startInvocation with the identical request and then with different inputs
expect: the identical retry yields the same semanticRequestDigest, so the platform Idempotency-Key=start:{ownershipId} never false-conflicts
the identical retry yields the same remoteSessionRef/remoteExecutionRef, satisfying the protocol rule that a duplicate start returns the original refs
changed business content yields a different semanticRequestDigest, so a real conflict is detectable
platform-side intent freezing and StartIntentConflict are proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision whose execution.started callback may arrive before the HTTP acknowledgement
required_cases.when: the Publication runner inspects the acknowledgement shape and its correlation key
expect: the acknowledgement contains only the protocol's transport-acceptance fields and never claims a run fact
the same start intent returns the same semanticRequestDigest, so an early callback is correlatable with the acknowledgement
platform-side Session pre-registration preceding any accepted callback is proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision replayed with the exact same start intent
required_cases.when: the Publication runner replays startInvocation with the identical request
expect: the replay yields the same semanticRequestDigest as the original start
the replay yields the same capabilitiesDigest as the original start and equals the published capability manifest digest, so the original receipt never drifts
platform-side exact event receipt (eventId/sequence/payloadHash/Attempt/Ownership/Epoch) and rejection of new events from an old owner are proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision receiving a control command carrying an older lease epoch
required_cases.when: handleSteer is invoked with a stale-generation AuthorityIdentity
expect: the runtime either rejects the command by an authority decision (NotCurrentExecutor / OwnershipExpired / AttemptMismatch / RuntimeSessionMismatch)
or, if it accepts, the acknowledgement echoes exactly the same target generation and never re-targets the command to another generation
a rejection for any other reason (control service not wired, transport failure) is inconclusive and fails the case
platform-side generation fencing in requireCurrentExecutionAuthority is proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision declaring a workspace profile
required_cases.when: the Publication runner starts the adapter once per declared mode and once with an undeclared mode
expect: every declared workspaceModes entry is accepted by a real startInvocation
a mode the runtime does not declare is rejected (fail closed), never silently accepted
a runtime can never pass by declaring all booleans true while accepting profiles it does not declare
platform-side WorkspaceBinding/Writer transaction and fence evidence is proven by platform integration conformance

required_cases.given: a candidate RuntimeRevision that may or may not declare a checkpoint-restorable workspace
required_cases.when: the Publication runner checks the declared workspace profile and, only when declared, probes resume
expect: when CHECKPOINT_RESTORABLE is not declared, the runner only verifies it is not advertised; the case passes without fabricating a resume call
when CHECKPOINT_RESTORABLE is declared, the runner performs a real handleResume carrying a checkpointRef and requires an accepted acknowledgement with non-empty remote refs
the specific snapshot behaviour is only required of a runtime that actually declares the capability
